correctness.rationale: A complete orbit proof shows the tested binomial quotient has denominator at most two and never fails for even n. Kummer gives an exact if-and-only-if in terms of the 3n+1 trailing-one depth. Seven explicit deterministic carry states capture the entire unrestricted future zero tail. Exact integer-polynomial equations H_i=Q t_i+z sum H_j prove the rational generating function formally; initial values and recurrence follow. The primitive four-state block supports the simple dominant eigenvalue and the stated density conclusion. The actual standalone verify.py executes and checks all polynomial equations and independent finite cases, without mistaking finite sampling for proof.

originality.rationale: Sun 2010 proves a divisor with a potential factor-of-two obstruction and proposes examining nondivisibility; Guo and Krattenthaler 2013 prove infinitely many failures in the relevant (2,3) family but do not enumerate failures at dyadic scales. The closest accessible unpublished prior result on the precise (5,2) binomial ray proves its marginal valuation distribution only; it lacks the simultaneous valuation threshold 3n+1. This finding solves the joint event and derives a rational series, recurrence, growth exponent and density zero. Targeted published-finding corpus and web literature searches did not locate a covering claim. This is a best-knowledge assessment, not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The question is the natural quantitative form of an exception problem explicitly posed by Sun and resolved only qualitatively by Guo–Krattenthaler. An exact dyadic census and noninteger growth exponent quantify the sparseness of the infinitely many failures, which cannot be inferred from the existing qualitative theorem or the marginal binomial valuation histogram. The varying-divisor carry threshold is the mathematical substance, not an arbitrary renaming or a fixed numerical cutoff.
